course: Cosmetics: Lip Balms, Body Butters & Hair Oils
module_title: Sourcing and Preparing African Raw Materials

lessons.title: Identifying Quality Shea Nuts and Shea Butter
lessons.body:
Shea butter comes from the nuts of the shea tree, which grows wild across West Africa. To get high-quality butter, start with good nuts. Harvest shea fruits when they fall to the ground naturallyâusually from June to August. Pick fruits that are yellow-green and soft. Remove the pulp and wash the nuts. Boil the nuts for 30 minutes to kill germs and loosen the shell. Crack the shells with a stone or hammer. The kernel inside should be white or light cream, not dark or mouldy. Spread kernels in the sun for 3-5 days until they are completely dry. They should rattle when shaken and break easily, not bend.

To make shea butter, grind dried kernels into a paste using a mill or mortar and pestle. Add a little water and knead the paste for 20-30 minutes until it becomes smooth and sticky. You can also roast the paste lightly before kneading to get a nuttier smell. Then boil the paste with water in a large pot. The oil will float to the top. Skim it off and strain through a cloth. Repeat boiling and skimming until no more oil comes. Let the oil cool and solidify. Good shea butter is ivory or pale yellow, has a mild nutty smell, and melts on your skin without feeling greasy. It should not smell rancid or have black particles. Store in a clean, dry container away from sunlight. In Africa, you can sell unrefined shea butter to local cosmetic makers or export it. Always wear gloves when handling raw nuts to avoid stains.

lessons.title: Harvesting and Drying Cocoa Pods for Cocoa Butter
lessons.body:
Cocoa butter is the fat from cocoa beans. It is solid at room temperature but melts on skin, making it perfect for lip balms and body butters. In Africa, cocoa grows in countries like Ghana, CÃ´te d'Ivoire, and Nigeria. Harvest pods when they turn yellow or orangeâusually 5-6 months after flowering. Cut the pod from the tree with a sharp machete or knife, being careful not to damage the branch. Open the pod by hitting it with a wooden club. Scoop out the white pulp and beans. Do not eat the beans raw; they are bitter.

Fermentation is key to flavour and quality. Put beans and pulp in a heap on banana leaves or in a wooden box. Cover with more leaves and let them ferment for 5-7 days. Turn the beans every 2 days. After fermentation, wash the beans to remove pulp. Then dry them in the sun on a raised mat or concrete floor for 7-10 days. Stir them every few hours. They are dry when they are brown, brittle, and make a cracking sound when you bite one. Moisture should be below 8%. Store dried beans in jute bags in a dry room.

To extract cocoa butter, roast dried beans at 120-140Â°C for 30-45 minutes. Cool and remove shells. Grind the nibs into a paste (cocoa liquor). Press the paste in a manual or hydraulic press to squeeze out cocoa butter. The butter is golden-yellow and smells like chocolate. Filter it through a fine cloth. Pour into moulds and let it harden. One kilogram of dried beans gives about 400-500 grams of cocoa butter. Use it in lip balms, body butters, and hair oils. Store in a cool, dark place. Rancidity happens if exposed to heat or light, so keep it sealed.

lessons.title: Extracting Oil from Coconut and Palm Kernel
lessons.body:
Coconut and palm kernel oils are staples in African cosmetics. They are light, absorb quickly, and have natural vitamin E. To extract coconut oil, use mature coconutsâbrown and hairy. Crack them open with a hammer or stone. Scoop out the white meat and grate it finely. Mix the grated coconut with warm water (about 1 part coconut to 2 parts water) and squeeze the mixture through a clean cloth. Collect the milky liquid. Let it sit for 4-6 hours. The oil will separate and float. Skim it off. You can also boil the milk gently for 20 minutes; the oil will rise. Strain and store in a bottle. Cold-pressed coconut oil is white and solid below 24Â°C. One coconut gives about 100-150 ml of oil. For larger batches, use a mechanical press.

Palm kernel oil comes from the seeds inside palm fruits. After harvesting palm fruits, separate the kernels from the fibrous pulp. Wash and dry kernels in the sun for 2-3 days. Crack the shells with a nutcracker or stone. The kernel inside is white. Grind kernels into a paste. Mix with water and boil for 30 minutes. The oil will float. Skim and strain. You can also use a press for better yield. Palm kernel oil is white to pale yellow, solid at room temperature, and has a mild nutty smell. One kilogram of kernels gives about 400-500 ml of oil. Both oils are great for hair and skin. Store in dark glass bottles away from heat. If oil smells sour or turns cloudy, it has gone bad. Always label with date.

lessons.title: Using Moringa, Baobab, and Marula Oils
lessons.body:
Moringa, baobab, and marula are three African trees that give excellent oils for cosmetics. Moringa oil comes from the seeds of the moringa tree, which grows in many parts of Africa. Collect mature seed pods when they turn brown and dry. Remove seeds and winnow to remove chaff. Cold-press the seeds or grind them and boil with water to float the oil. Moringa oil is clear, light yellow, and absorbs fast. It is rich in oleic acid and antioxidants. Use it for face serums, hair oils, and lip balms. One kilogram of seeds yields about 300-400 ml of oil. Store in a cool, dark place; it stays fresh for 1-2 years.

Baobab oil comes from the seeds inside the hard fruit of the baobab tree. Harvest fruits when they fall from the tree. Crack the hard shell with a hammer. Remove the white, powdery pulp (which you can eat) and the black seeds. Dry seeds in the sun for 2-3 days. Crack the seed coat and extract the kernel. Grind kernels into a paste and press or boil to extract oil. Baobab oil is golden-yellow, thick, and has a nutty smell. It is high in vitamins A, D, E, and F. Use it for stretch marks, dry skin, and hair conditioning. One kilogram of kernels gives about 250-300 ml of oil. It can solidify in cold weather; warm the bottle in your hands.

Marula oil comes from the kernels of marula fruits, found in southern Africa. Harvest fallen fruits, remove the pulp (which can be used for juice), and crack the hard nuts to get kernels. Dry kernels, then cold-press or boil to extract oil. Marula oil is clear, light, and absorbs quickly. It is rich in oleic acid and antioxidants. Use it for face and body oils, and as a carrier oil for essential oils. One kilogram of kernels yields about 300-400 ml of oil. All three oils should be stored in dark glass bottles away from sunlight. Test for rancidity by smellingâif it smells like crayons or old nuts, discard.

lessons.title: Cleaning and Sterilizing Containers and Tools
lessons.body:
Clean containers and tools are critical for cosmetics. Dirty equipment introduces bacteria, mould, and yeast that spoil your products and harm skin. Start by washing all toolsâspoons, bowls, pots, blenders, and containersâwith hot water and dish soap. Use a bottle brush for narrow jars. Rinse thoroughly to remove all soap. For sterilization, you have three easy methods. First, boiling: put glass jars, metal tools, and heat-safe plastic in a large pot of water. Bring to a boil for 10 minutes. Remove with clean tongs and air-dry on a clean cloth. Second, steaming: use a food steamer or a pot with a colander insert. Steam for 15 minutes. Third, oven: heat oven to 120Â°C. Place clean, dry glass jars and metal tools on a baking tray. Heat for 20 minutes. Do not put plastic in the oven.

After sterilization, handle items with clean hands or tongs. Do not touch the inside of containers. Let them cool completely before filling with oils or butters. For pumps and droppers, disassemble and boil the parts. For plastic containers that cannot be boiled, wash with hot soapy water, rinse, then wipe with 70% alcohol and let air-dry. Always work on a clean surface. Wear gloves and a face mask if you have one. Sterilize your workspace with alcohol spray. After filling, seal containers tightly. Label with product name and date. Store in a cool, dark place. If you see cloudiness, mould, or a bad smell, throw the product away. Clean equipment after every use to prevent build-up. In Africa, you can use a solar oven for sterilization if you have oneâit reaches 120Â°C and saves fuel.

lessons.title: Storing Raw Materials to Prevent Rancidity
lessons.body:
Rancidity is the enemy of natural oils and butters. It happens when oxygen, heat, or light break down fats, causing a bad smell and skin irritation. To prevent it, store raw materials properly. First, keep everything in dark glass or food-grade plastic containers with tight lids. Clear plastic lets light in, so avoid it. Second, store in a cool, dark placeâideally below 25Â°C. A cupboard away from the stove is good. In hot African climates, a root cellar or a cool room works. You can also use a refrigerator for long-term storage, but let items come to room temperature before use to avoid condensation.

Third, minimize air exposure. Fill containers to the top to reduce headspace. Use smaller containers if you open them often. For solid butters like shea and cocoa, scoop out what you need with a clean, dry spoon and reseal immediately. Do not double-dip. Fourth, add natural antioxidants. A few drops of vitamin E oil (1% of total weight) or rosemary extract can extend shelf life. You can also add 0.5% of citric acid to water-based products, but not to pure oils. Fifth, label everything with the date you opened or made it. Use older stock first. Sixth, keep a log of smells and textures. If an oil smells like crayons, old nuts, or feels sticky, it is rancid. Throw it awayâdo not use it on skin.

Shelf life varies: shea butter lasts 1-2 years; cocoa butter 2-5 years; coconut oil 2 years; palm kernel oil 1 year; moringa, baobab, and marula oils 1-2 years. Heat and light shorten these times. In Africa, you can store in clay pots in a cool roomâclay keeps temperature stable. Always keep containers sealed when not in use. For long-term storage, you can freeze butters in airtight bags; they last indefinitely. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature, to avoid moisture. By following these steps, you protect your raw materials and your final products.

quiz.q: What color should high-quality shea kernels be inside?
quiz.explanation: Good shea kernels are white or light cream; dark or mouldy kernels indicate poor quality.

quiz.q: How long should shea nuts be boiled to kill germs and loosen shells?
quiz.explanation: Boiling for 30 minutes is recommended to sterilize and soften the shells.

quiz.q: What is a sign that dried shea kernels are ready for storage?
options: B) They rattle when shaken and break easily
C) They are soft and sticky
quiz.explanation: Dry kernels rattle and break easily; if they bend, they still have moisture.

quiz.q: How long should cocoa beans ferment?
quiz.explanation: Fermentation for 5-7 days develops flavor and quality.

quiz.q: What moisture content should dried cocoa beans have?
quiz.explanation: Beans should be dried to below 8% moisture to prevent mould.

quiz.q: How much cocoa butter can you get from 1 kg of dried cocoa beans?
quiz.explanation: About 400-500 g of cocoa butter is extracted from 1 kg of beans.

quiz.q: What part of the coconut is used to extract coconut oil?
quiz.explanation: The white meat is grated and squeezed to extract coconut oil.

quiz.q: How long should you let coconut milk sit to separate oil?
quiz.explanation: Letting it sit for 4-6 hours allows the oil to separate and float.

quiz.q: What color is palm kernel oil?
quiz.explanation: Palm kernel oil is white to pale yellow and solid at room temperature.

quiz.q: How much oil can you get from 1 kg of palm kernels?
quiz.explanation: About 400-500 ml of oil is extracted from 1 kg of kernels.

quiz.q: Which tree produces seeds used for moringa oil?
quiz.explanation: Moringa oil comes from the seeds of the moringa tree.

quiz.q: What is a key property of moringa oil?
options: A) It is thick and greasy
B) It absorbs quickly and is rich in antioxidants
C) It solidifies at room temperature
D) It has a strong perfume smell
quiz.explanation: Moringa oil is light, absorbs fast, and contains antioxidants.

quiz.q: How much oil can you get from 1 kg of moringa seeds?
quiz.explanation: About 300-400 ml of moringa oil is extracted from 1 kg of seeds.

quiz.q: Which part of the baobab fruit contains the seeds for oil?
quiz.explanation: The seeds are inside the hard shell of the baobab fruit.

quiz.q: What color is baobab oil?
quiz.explanation: Baobab oil is golden-yellow and thick.

quiz.q: Which vitamin is NOT typically high in baobab oil?
quiz.explanation: Baobab oil is rich in vitamins A, D, E, and F, but not vitamin C.

quiz.q: Where is marula oil traditionally sourced?
quiz.explanation: Marula oil comes from marula fruits found in southern Africa.

quiz.q: How much oil can you get from 1 kg of marula kernels?
quiz.explanation: About 300-400 ml of marula oil is extracted from 1 kg of kernels.

quiz.q: Why is it important to sterilize containers and tools?
options: A) To make them look shiny
B) To prevent bacteria and mould that spoil products
quiz.explanation: Sterilization kills microbes that cause spoilage and skin infections.

quiz.q: How long should glass jars be boiled to sterilize?
quiz.explanation: Boiling for 10 minutes is sufficient to sterilize glass jars.

quiz.q: What temperature should an oven be set to for sterilizing glass jars?
quiz.explanation: Heating at 120Â°C for 20 minutes sterilizes glass and metal tools.

quiz.q: Which method is NOT suitable for sterilizing plastic containers?
quiz.explanation: Plastic can melt in the oven; use boiling, steaming, or alcohol instead.

quiz.q: What should you do after sterilizing containers?
options: A) Touch the inside with bare hands
B) Let them cool and handle with clean tongs
quiz.explanation: Handle with clean tongs and let cool to avoid recontamination.

quiz.q: What causes rancidity in oils and butters?
options: A) Exposure to oxygen, heat, and light
quiz.explanation: Oxygen, heat, and light break down fats, causing rancidity.

quiz.q: What is a good storage temperature for raw materials?
quiz.explanation: Cool temperatures below 25Â°C slow down rancidity.

quiz.q: How can you minimize air exposure in storage containers?
options: A) Fill containers to the top
quiz.explanation: Filling containers to the top reduces headspace and oxygen exposure.

quiz.q: What natural antioxidant can be added to extend shelf life?
quiz.explanation: Vitamin E oil (1% of total weight) helps prevent rancidity.

quiz.q: What is the shelf life of shea butter if stored properly?
quiz.explanation: Shea butter lasts 1-2 years when stored in a cool, dark place.

quiz.q: What is a sign that an oil is rancid?
options: A) It smells like crayons or old nuts
B) It is clear and golden
D) It has a nutty smell
quiz.explanation: Rancid oil smells like crayons or old nuts and should be discarded.

quiz.q: How can you store butters for long-term preservation?
quiz.explanation: Freezing in airtight bags preserves butters for long periods.
